corpusSummary: This corpus assembles 2026 social-science inquiries into large language models across health, education, governance, and everyday use, highlighting trust, ethics, safety, and equity; methodological innovations include AI-assisted research tools, multi-agent simulations, and AI-enabled analysis of policy, education, heritage, and communication. The records reveal ongoing concerns about anthropomorphism, mis/disinformation, and the need for governance, transparency, and human-in-the-loop verification.

themes.name: Trust, perception, and ethics in AI-enabled interaction
themes.description: Explores how users perceive AI, the role of humanness vs. empathy, and ethical risks in AI-enabled decision-making and everyday interactions.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: literacy, pedagogy, safety, and assessment
themes.description: Examines AI's impact on learning, AI literacy, classroom scaffolding, tutoring, and the redesign of assessment practices in diverse educational contexts.

themes.name: AI as a research tool and methodological innovation in social science
themes.description: Documents how LLMs and AI agents are used for data analysis, coding, simulations, and governance, with emphasis on validation and ethical scrutiny.

themes.name: Equity, bias, fairness, and governance in AI deployment
themes.description: Centers on equitable AI use in health, libraries, policy research, and global contexts, including frameworks to audit safety, cultural adequacy, and bias mitigation.
